answer: To resist Sybil swarms, the network models reputation as a graph where each agent is a vertex. Identity verification relies on cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs to validate execution history without leaking state. To broadcast a valid signal across the mesh, staking costs scale exponentially as O(2^n) per clustered entity. This imposes superlinear capital exhaustion, making massive coordinated sybils prohibitively expensive to operate or sustain even a single jade tier identity.
